title: SMIC raises prices as AI demand pushes fabs past 93% utilization
subtitle: China's largest foundry tops $3B quarterly revenue for the first time as AI infrastructure tightens capacity well beyond Nvidia-class chips.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation, China's largest chip foundry, is raising prices on its most sought-after manufacturing capacity as AI-related demand keeps its factories running near the ceiling. SMIC's Q2 utilization hit 93.7%, quarterly revenue topped $3 billion for the first time, and quarterly profit more than tripled year-over-year to $479.2 million. The company is signaling further price increases through the rest of 2026.

The specific chips are not the frontier AI accelerators — SMIC does not compete with TSMC on the leading nodes — but everything around them. Memory controllers, power-management ICs, networking silicon, and the mature-node parts that go into every rack of AI infrastructure are all in short supply as the buildout continues. It is the second-order effect of the AI capex cycle: the visible bottleneck is Nvidia B300 supply, but the bottleneck under that is the boring silicon that makes an AI data center actually turn on.

For China's semiconductor sector specifically, the tightening is a policy tailwind. Domestic foundries have spent five years being squeezed by U.S. export controls; the same AI capex cycle that made Nvidia the world's most valuable company is now filling the order books of the fabs those controls were meant to slow. SMIC's numbers are the clearest datapoint yet that the AI-infrastructure demand shock is a global equalizer, not just a Silicon Valley bull market.

Takeaway for learners: when a supply chain is under stress, the choke point moves. This year the constraint is not GPUs, it is the mature-node silicon and the power infrastructure to plug it in. If you are building AI products, the practical implication is that latency, cost, and reliability of hosted inference will be shaped less by which foundation model you pick and more by which cloud region can actually get a rack online this quarter. Watch capacity announcements, not benchmark scores.
